name: FAPI Validation
description: Declarative Form API validation and filtering framework: attach reusable validator and filter rules to form elements by name via #validators and #filters instead of hand-writing #element_validate callbacks.
project_description: FAPI Validation extends Drupal's Form API with a declarative validation and input-filtering layer, so developers attach reusable checks and transforms to a form element by name instead of writing bespoke #element_validate callbacks. hook_element_info_alter registers FapiValidationService::process on every input element; at render time that process callback appends FapiValidationService::filter and FapiValidationService::validate to the element's #element_validate when the element declares #filters or #validators. Two Drupal plugin types drive it: FapiValidationValidator plugins (bundled: numeric, alpha, alpha_numeric, alpha_dash, digit, decimal, limit_decimals, length, chars, email, url, ipv4, regexp, match_field, range) return a boolean pass/fail and carry a default error_message or error_callback in their attribute; FapiValidationFilter plugins (bundled: numeric, trim, ltrim, rtrim, machine_name, ucfirst, ucwords, uppercase, lowercase, strip_tags, html_entities) transform the submitted value before validation. Rules are written as a plain id ('email'), an id with bracketed parameters ('length[10, 50]', 'range[0, 100]', 'regexp[/^.../]'), or an array with 'rule' plus a per-rule 'error' message or 'error callback'. The Validator value object parses each rule into a name and parameter list. An admin settings form (route fapi_validation.settings at /admin/config/system/fapi, permission 'manage fapi validation settings') exposes a single 'bypass' flag stored in fapi_validation.settings config; when enabled it lets users holding the 'bypass fapi validations' permission (or a per-validator 'bypass <id> fapi validation' permission generated by FapiValidationPermissions) skip validation. Two read-only controller routes list the registered validator and filter plugins. Custom validator/filter plugins are added by any module by dropping a class under Plugin/FapiValidationValidator or Plugin/FapiValidationFilter. Ships an example submodule, fapiv_example.
